Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear ask. Putting a short commercial + technical sketch below and looping in Marcus (solutions) for the quant/quality guidance. I'm attaching a concise pricing summary (redwood_optimize_pricing_v3.pdf).

High level (very rough numbers for 450-token avg):
- Batching + caching first: typically reduces effective token cost 25–45% for assistant-style workloads with stable prompts (prefix caching + KV reuse). Latency improves for tails when batching is tuned, but peak p95 can increase if batch windows are too long.
- Quantization (int8 / 4-bit combos): additional 10–35% CPU/GPU cost reduction depending on model family and quality target; 4-bit gives larger gains but risks small regressions on subtle generation quality unless VEQ (evals) are in place.

Recommended packaging options (summary in attached PDF):
A) Pay-as-you-go: list pricing + Optimize recommendations. Good for pilots; no commitment.
B) Committed credits (6–12 months): volume tiers, typical discount 10–20% vs PAYG; Optimize guidance + batching tuning included.
C) Enterprise Reserved (Dedicated GPU pools + SLO): baseline commit with higher discounts (20–30%), on-call engineering support, and quantization profiling + on-prem tuning included in SOW.

Marcus — can you add the technical delta for 4-bit vs int8 for Llama2-style family and call out our safe-guarding evals?

Deliverables we can share by EOD: one-page mutual action plan, pricing PDF (attached), and a SOW skeleton. If procurement wants stronger concession (e.g., 20%+ off) we'll need a committed ARR and SOW commitment.

Laura / Ellen — quick technical notes based on SproutAI's footprint (450-token avg, high QPS):

1) Baseline (no quant, minimal caching): cost = X (reference). Latency best but unit cost highest.

2) Batching + prefix/KV caching:
- If 40–60% of tokens are repeated prefixes (chat system prompts), you can expect 20–40% cost reduction out of the gate from prefix + KV cache saving requests to the model.
- Continuous batching yields 10–25% more savings on peak-throughput runs but requires careful latency SLO tuning.

3) Quantization impact:
- int8: ~8–18% additional cost reduction vs baseline, minimal quality delta on mainstream LLMs with our quant kernels.
- 4-bit (Q4_0 / Q4_K): ~18–35% additional reduction but quality regressions possible on hallucination-sensitive tasks.
- Hybrid approach: apply int8 to safety-critical routes; enable 4-bit for bulk reranking or non-critical assistants.

4) Operational cost: quantization lowers GPU memory and allows higher packing, which may reduce the number of GPU instances required (multiplicative effect on cost). However, engineering validation (evals + A/B) is required before broad rollout.

I'll attach a quick CSV of recommended quant profiles per route for your review.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
